report.executive_summary: Autonomous threat hunt completed. Multiple ATT&CK techniques confirmed.

findings.title: Systematic Brute Force Attack Against Administrator Account
findings.description: 15 failed logon attempts (Event ID 4625) occurring between 2024-06-15 02:30:03 and 02:34:27, all targeting the CORP\Administrator account via network logon (LogonType 3). All attempts originate from the same source IP 192.168.1.105 with varying port numbers, indicating systematic password guessing attacks. The FailureReason "Unknown user name or bad password" confirms authentication failures.

findings.title: PowerShell-Based Defense Evasion - Windows Defender Disabled
findings.description: Multiple PowerShell commands executed to disable Windows Defender real-time monitoring and behavior monitoring. Event ID 4688 at 02:44:54 shows "powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true" and Event ID 4688 at 02:55:58 shows additional parameters "-DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true". Additionally, Event ID 13 at 02:56:28 shows registry modification to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\DisableAntiSpyware, confirming persistent defense evasion attempt.
evidence: Event ID 4688 at 02:44:54 - powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true
Event ID 4688 at 02:55:58 - powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true
Event ID 13 at 02:56:28 - Registry modification to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\DisableAntiSpyware
Event ID 1102 at 03:15:04 - Security audit log was cleared by Administrator
Defense mechanisms systematically disabled during same timeframe as malicious activities

findings.title: Credential Dumping via LSASS Process Memory Extraction
findings.description: Procdump.exe utility executed at 2024-06-15T02:49:27 with command "procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp" to extract the full memory dump of the LSASS process. This is preceded by reconnaissance at 02:46:20 with command "powershell.exe -c 'Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'lsass'}'" to locate the LSASS process. Event ID 10 (Sysmon process access) at 02:49:11 shows PowerShell accessing lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1010, confirming credential dumping attempt.

findings.title: Malicious Lateral Movement via SMB with Embedded Credentials
findings.description: Event ID 4688 at 2024-06-15T03:01:45 shows execution of "net use \\192.168.1.110\C$ /user:Administrator Lab123!" - an attempt to establish SMB connection to remote host 192.168.1.110 with Administrator credentials. This is corroborated by Sysmon Event ID 3 at 03:01:37 showing net.exe initiating TCP connection to 192.168.1.115:445 and another connection to 192.168.1.110:445 at 03:03:47. The presence of plaintext password "Lab123!" in command line indicates attacker attempting lateral movement with guessed/compromised credentials.
evidence: Event ID 4688 at 03:01:45 - net use command with embedded credentials to 192.168.1.110
Event ID 3 at 03:01:37 - Sysmon network connection from net.exe to 192.168.1.115:445 (SMB)
Event ID 3 at 03:03:47 - Sysmon network connection from net.exe to 192.168.1.110:445 (SMB)
Plaintext password 'Lab123!' exposed in command line arguments
Multiple simultaneous SMB connection attempts to different hosts indicates systematic lateral movement

findings.title: PowerShell Command Execution for Reconnaissance and Malware Delivery
findings.description: Multiple PowerShell command executions detected for reconnaissance and potential malware delivery. Event ID 4688 at 02:42:42 shows execution of AtomicRedTeam framework ("powershell.exe -exec bypass -c 'Import-Module C:\AtomicRedTeam\invoke-atomicredteam\Invoke-Atom..."). Event ID 4688 at 02:43:19 shows IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString command for downloading remote code execution. Additional reconnaissance commands include ipconfig, systeminfo, whoami, hostname, and net user executed from PowerShell. Registry modification at 03:06:20 shows persistence mechanism via HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\WindowsUpdate. Event ID 4698 at 02:53:15 shows scheduled task creation "UpdateCheck" with hidden PowerShell command containing IEX invocation.
evidence: Event ID 4688 at 02:42:42 - Import-Module C:\AtomicRedTeam\invoke-atomicredteam\Invoke-Atom... with -exec bypass
Event ID 4688 at 02:43:19 - IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString for code download
Event ID 4688 at 02:45:26 - ipconfig /all executed from PowerShell
Event ID 4688 at 02:46:13 - net user reconnaissance from PowerShell
Event ID 4688 at 02:46:20 - Get-Process piped to find lsass.exe
Event ID 4698 at 02:53:15 - Scheduled task \Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\UpdateCheck with hidden PowerShell -NoP -W Hidden -c IEX
Event ID 13 at 03:06:20 - Registry Run key modified to C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\...
Systematic use of -NoP -W Hidden -Exec Bypass flags indicates obfuscation attempts

findings.title: Security Log Tampering - Audit Log Cleared
findings.description: Event ID 1102 at 2024-06-15T03:15:04 indicates the security audit log was cleared by the Administrator account in the CORP domain. This log clearing occurred at the end of the attack timeline (03:15:04), which is after all major malicious activities (which concluded around 03:06:20). The timing suggests deliberate evidence destruction to cover tracks of the compromise.
evidence: Event ID 1102 at 03:15:04 - The audit log was cleared by CORP\Administrator
Log clearing occurred after completion of malicious activities, suggesting deliberate evidence destruction
Timing correlates with end of attack timeline (latest suspicious activity at 03:06:20)
